messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - GPU_POOL_SATURATION detected in us-west-2. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit max_replicas. Affected model(s): model-v22. Timestamp: 3512345678. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3512345678

deploy-bot: Deploy v22 started 14m ago by @david, rollout strategy: canary 20% -> 100% over 30m. commit: a1b2c3d.

alexa (eng-runtime): I'm taking this thread. Seeing large queue growth on the v22 route, prefill/prefetch traffic looks amplified. Checking autoscaler logs now.

alexa (eng-runtime): quick snippet from autoscaler: ```ERROR autoscaler: cannot scale beyond max_replicas (20) reason=quota_exhausted current_replicas=20 pending_requests=842 queue_growth=73%```

alexa (eng-runtime): also runtime logs show many long-context requests warming kv-cache for v22, avg_seq_len jumped from 512 -> 2400 in the last 10m.

david (eng-ml): we rolled a tokenization change + larger system prefix in v22 to improve summarization quality. didn't expect prefill amplification. sounds like kv-cache warming + longer sequences doubled GPU memory/time per request.

samir (eng-oncall): I'm paging SRE and infra. @kyle can you look at pool quota and whether we can temporarily lift max_replicas? If not, we need traffic mitigation ASAP. Customer impact: increased latency and 429s.

kyle (eng-sre): looking. AWS quotas won't let us add GPUs in this pool instantly. We can either 1) divert traffic to fallback model v21, 2) decrease concurrency/burst on v22, or 3) manually move some reservations from non-critical pools (takes ~8-12m). Which do we want?

alexa (eng-runtime): quick mitigation plan: 1) route 60% of traffic to v21 fallback, 2) enable prefill backoff on v22, 3) increase autoscaler max_replicas to 30 as a temporary emergency if quota allows. I'll submit patch for routing now.

support-ops: Affected customers: AcmePayments (sev=high, realtime chat has >50% error), EduSage (sev=medium, embeddings delayed), BrightForms (sev=low). CS oncall notified @customer-success.

alexa (eng-runtime): executing routing patch: ```curl -X POST https://runtime.redwood/api/routes/patch -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" -d '{"route":"/v22","weight":{"v22":0.4,"v21":0.6}}'``` applying... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incidents-bot: Status changed -> mitigating.

alexa (eng-runtime): applied. Confirming traffic shift in gateway metrics. Initial checks show 60% of requests now hitting v21.

kyle (eng-sre): queue length starting to drop, pending_requests -> 260 (was 842). latency P95 for v22 still elevated but trending down. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/cluster/gpu-pool-usw2?orgId=1

david (eng-ml): rolling back the system prompt would be risky (quality regression). Recommend keep fallback routing and throttle prefill. We should also add kv-cache warmup limits to the model config.

samir (eng-oncall): handing oncall to @kyle for mitigation and monitoring. Handoff note: samir -> kyle at 14:05 UTC. I will monitor customer comms. :point_up:

kyle (eng-sre): taking over. I'll request emergency quota increase from cloud infra and open manual reservation, but that takes time. For now I'll keep routing and set a conservative concurrency cap for v22: ```SET_ROUTE_CONCURRENCY v22 8```

alexa (eng-runtime): implemented concurrency cap and prefill backoff flag: ```PATCH /models/v22/config {"prefill_backoff_ms":200,"max_concurrency":8}``` applied. Requests queued but not causing GPU OOMs.

audit-bot: Action logged: route patch by alexa@eng, config patch by alexa@eng, concurrency set by kyle@eng-sre. AuditID: audit-3512345678-1

support-ops: CS notified top-ten customers, sending status update and mitigation notes. AcmePayments is routing to v21 and reporting degraded but functional.

kyle (eng-sre): autoscaler request for max_replicas bump submitted to infra: ticket INF-8801. If approved we can restore capacity and gradually increase v22 traffic back to canary levels.

alexa (eng-runtime): quick root cause summary: model-v22 introduced larger system prefix + tokenizer change; many customers trigger long context prefill path which warms kv-cache aggressively. This increases per-request GPU time and memory footprint, causing autoscaler to hit configured max_replicas and queue to grow.

david (eng-ml): agreed. We'll prepare a small model patch to limit prefill kv growth and a canary flag to gate tokenizer change.

support-ops: Current impact: 3 customers high/medium reduced quality and increased latency, ~2% impact on total request volume. No data loss.

kyle (eng-sre): monitoring for 30m then we'll decide to either slowly ramp v22 back or revert the deploy. For now mitigation = keep route weights at v21 60%, v22 40% and keep concurrency cap.

customer-success: prepping customer-facing postmortem snippet and next steps: we'll communicate timeline once infra quota decision is in.

alexa (eng-runtime): switching incident channel tag to #incident-live, creating follow-up ticket to add automatic prefill detection to rollout gates and add autoscaler emergency policy to temporarily increase quota.

kyle (eng-sre): small update: queue stable at ~120 pending, P95 latency improving, no OOMs. Keeping handoff. If we see second spike we'll escalate to infra on-call.

samir (eng-oncall): thanks team. I'll capture the timeline and initial impact for the postmortem. Next steps: 1) patch model to reduce prefill size, 2) add rollout canary checks measuring avg_seq_len & kv-cache churn, 3) update runbook to include route-diversion recipe.

incidents-bot: Incident P1 - mitigating -> monitoring. Updated severity: P1 -> P2 after mitigation.

alexa (eng-runtime): marking this thread for post-incident cleanup. I'll attach logs and config diffs to INF-8801. :white_check_mark:

kyle (eng-sre): handing back to oncall rotation: kyle -> night-oncall at 15:00 UTC. I'll leave monitoring alerts with extended thresholds for 4h.

---
Post-incident notes (summary to paste into ticket): 1) Cause: v22 rollout increased average sequence length and kv-cache warmups -> per-request GPU cost increase. 2) Mitigation: traffic diversion to v21 fallback, prefill backoff + concurrency cap, manual infra quota request. 3) Customer impact: temporary latency/429s for a handful of customers, no data loss. 4) Action items: add rollout gate for kv-cache metrics, implement per-model prefill limits, emergency autoscaler quota playbook, include tokenization changes in canary gating.
